paraphrase: 'He' is great compassion and 'vajra' is wisdom; hear the tantra of Hevajra, the union of the two, spoken by the Lord.

paraphrase: Caṇḍālī blazes at the navel; she burns the five tathāgatas and Locanā and the other goddesses; when she is burnt the moon (the syllable HAṂ at the head) melts.
notes: Hevajra Sanskrit not available locally; Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Summary only.

paraphrase: Of the thirty-two channels three are principal: lalanā on the left (wisdom, moon), rasanā on the right (means, sun) and avadhūtī in the centre, free of the duality of grasped and grasper; four cakras — of emanation at the navel, of dharma at the heart, of enjoyment at the throat and of great bliss at the head.
notes: Hevajra Sanskrit not available locally; Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Verse numbers not fixed (c. I.1.12–31).

paraphrase: The four joys — joy, supreme joy, the joy of cessation and the innate joy — are correlated with the four moments (variety, ripening, dissolution, the signless) and the innate is known in the moment between supreme joy and cessation.
notes: Hevajra Sanskrit not available locally; Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Chapter uncertain (the joys are treated in I.1, I.8 and I.10); summary only.

paraphrase: There is no meditator and nothing meditated, no mantra and no deity; mantra and deity abide in the nature free of elaboration.
notes: Hevajra Sanskrit not available locally; Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Recalled as I.5.1 (book 1, ch. 5).

paraphrase: The observance (caryā) — wandering in solitary places and cremation grounds, eating what is given, with the ornaments of the heruka — is to be undertaken when one has attained some warmth (ūṣmā) in meditation.
notes: Hevajra Sanskrit not available locally; Reference from memory; not located in a local text.

paraphrase: The sacred sites — pīṭha, upapīṭha, kṣetra, upakṣetra, chandoha, upachandoha, melāpaka, upamelāpaka, śmaśāna, upaśmaśāna — are named and correlated with the ten bodhisattva grounds.
notes: Hevajra Sanskrit not available locally; Reference from memory; not located in a local text.

paraphrase: The innate is not told by another nor found anywhere; it is known by oneself through merit and attendance on the guru's feet.
notes: Hevajra Sanskrit not available locally; Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Recalled as I.8.36.

paraphrase: The world is bound by passion and by passion it is freed; this reversed meditation is not known by the Buddhist and non-Buddhist outsiders.
notes: Hevajra Sanskrit not available locally; Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Recalled as II.2.51.

paraphrase: The Lord teaches the 'intentional language' (sandhyābhāṣā), the great language of the yoginīs, a code of substitute words for substances, places and acts, which should not be revealed to the unconsecrated.

paraphrase: Beings are buddhas, but they are obscured by adventitious stains; when these are removed, they are buddhas.
